sections.text: Introduction

The purpose of this 
procedure is to provide detailed safe method for transmission lines maintenance 
staff to minimize the possibility of error causing personal injury or 
damage.
Safety Precautions

items:
Maintain the safe limits of approach 
 to energized conductors.

sections.text: Tools and Equipment

items:
Safety 
 personnel protective equipment.

Full 
 body harnesses.
Dynamometer.

sections.text: Work to be Carried Out

General Inspection 
before each use

items:
Before each 
 use carefully inspect the harness and associated equipment for signs of wear 
 or deterioration, or evidence of impact loading.

Visually 
 inspect for loose threads, pulled rivets, burns, cuts, abrasions, or evidence 
 of chemical or physical deterioration that may have weakened the material or 
 assembly.

Check all 
 snap hooks, buckles and D-rings for malfunctions and racks

Immediately destroy and replace any component 
 (warn/damaged), which does not pass inspection

sections.text: Harnesses Inspection

rows:
Inspect 
 the tongue and billet end first. They are subject to the most wear as a 
 result of repeated opening and closing. 
 If your harness is equipped with grommets, inspect for loose, broken or 
 distorted grommets.

Check 
 the Stitching for broken, burned, cut or pulled Stitches, 
 broken strands of webbing appears as tufts on the surface. 
 To 
 inspect, hold the harness with your hands six to eight inches apart. Bend 
 the webbing in an inverted "U" fashion to cause surface tension, exposing 
 problem areas, inspect the entire length of the webbing. Damage caused by 
 cuts, abrasions, corrosives, heat or chemicals should be apparent.

Check all 
 D-rings for distortion, D-ring attachment points 
 should be checked for unusual wear or damaged fibers. Badly D-rings indicate 
 chemical corrosion, and the equipment should be destroyed and replaced 
 immediately.

For stitched attachment points, check that stitching is not broken, burned, 
 cut or pulled.
 Check all riveted attachment points for tightness, especially those at 
 D-ring wear pads. Badly-pitted rivets indicate chemical corrosion, and the 
 equipment should be destroyed and replaced immediately.

Check 
 all tongue buckles for distortion, sharp edges and cracks. The tongue should 
 move freely and overlap the frame. Rollers should not be distorted and 
 should roll freely.

Check 
 all friction buckles for sharp edges, cracks, distortion and to see that 
 outer bars and centre bars are straight. Also check corners and attachment 
 points for wear and cracks.

If evidence of excessive wear, deterioration or mechanical malfunction is 
 observed, replace the harness immediately. Never work with worn or damaged 
 equipment. Using damaged or worn equipment can cause serous injury or 
 death.

sections.text: Important Note:

OSHA specifies that all covered by Occupational Safety and 
 Healthy act are responsible for inspection and maintenance of all tools and 
 equipment used by employees weather owned by the employees or by the 
 company. Personal protective equipment should be inspected before each use, 
 and immediately removed from service if any sign of wear or damage is found.
Maintenance Procedures

items:
Clean 
 and maintain equipment in accordance with recommended practice. Wash nylon 
 harness only in warm water and mild cleanser avoid harsh chemicals such as 
 degreasing compounds, turpentine, paint thinner, gasoline and other 
 solvents.

Allow 
 nylon objects to dry naturally. Dont use heat to speed up the process. 
 Inspect and lubricate all snap hooks after cleaning to make sure they 
 operate properly and close securely. Use Klein Cinch aerosol lubricant or 
 light motor oil.

sections.text: Read warning tags attached to your harness.

A set of warning tags and labels is attached to 
 each harness. For clarity, they are not shown in the illustrations in this 
 booklet. These highly durable warning and instruction tags/labels are 
 designed to be permanently attached. If they should become unattached or 
 damaged call the company.

Harnesses are for use by properly trained 
 professional only.
Looking hooks are Highly Recommended.

Always destroy harness if it has been 
 subjected to any impact loading.

Always visually check that all buckles 
 are properly closed before each use.
Always visually check that:

Each snap hock freely engages D-ring or anchor 
 point.

Keeper is completely closed before use. 
 Never rely only on the feel or sound of a snap hook engaging.

sections.text: Before each use check that:

Fabric is free of burns, cuts, broken stitches 
 or excessive wear
Rivets are not bent, loose or missing.

Buckles and D-rings are not distorted or 
 cracked.

If tongue buckle, tongue does not bind on 
 buckle and buckle holes are not damaged.

Remove from service and destroy harness if 
 it does not pass this inspection and replace immediately.

sections.text:
For personal use only, Not towing 
 or hoisting

Snap hooks attached to D-rings must have 
 less than 3/4'' (19mm) throat opening. Never attach ladder or rebar 
 hooks onto D-rings.

Only attach connecting devices meeting 
 government standards to D-rings.

Never attach foreign objects to D-rings. 
 They may prevent or falsely indicate snap hook engagement.

Never attach multiple snap hooks onto a 
 D-ring.

Never punch holes in or alter harness in 
 any way.

Never work without independent fall 
 arrest protection if there is danger of a fall.

Never rely on a retrieval or other 
 harness for fall arrest protection unless it has a fall arrest D-ring

During rebar work, always anchor the 
 positioning assembly hook to vertical reinforcing rods only.

Fall-arrest anchor points must support a 
 minimum of 5,000 Ibs (2,250kg) per attached worker and be independent of 
 worker support. Positioning, suspension or retrieval anchor points 
 must support your weight plus any job related load.

Test 
 the Full Body Harnesses Semi annually

Belt tension 
 test from waist 1200kg

Shoulders 
 and legs tension test 1000kg

Rope tension 
 test 1000kg

Hook tension 
 test 1000kg

Issue a 
 certificate that the harness and the rope pass the test.
